title: The invisible gorilla: why you miss what's right in front of you
description:
Simons and Chabris's famous 1999 experiment: about half of viewers never noticed a person in a gorilla suit. Here's how inattentional blindness works and why even expert experience doesn't protect you.
#psychology #attention #invisiblegorilla #shorts

scenes.narration: A gorilla walks right past, and half of people miss it.
scenes.imagePrompt: close-up of a gorilla face emerging from deep shadow, intense eyes, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: In nineteen ninety-nine, psychologists showed people a short video. Players in white and black shirts pass balls around.
scenes.imagePrompt: young people passing a basketball in a hallway, motion blur, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: The task is simple: carefully count how many passes the players in white make.
scenes.imagePrompt: players in white t-shirts passing a ball, focus on the ball, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Then a person in a gorilla suit walks into the middle of the court. Stops, beats its chest, and walks off.
scenes.imagePrompt: person in a gorilla costume walking between ball players, beating its chest, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: About half the viewers simply didn't see it. They were too busy counting passes.
scenes.imagePrompt: silhouettes of an audience staring at a bright screen in a dark room, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Expertise doesn't help. In twenty thirteen, a gorilla was inserted into lung scans, and eighty-three percent of radiologists missed it.

stat.label: of radiologists missed the gorilla on the scan

scenes.imagePrompt: radiologist examining lung scans on monitors in a dark reading room, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: It's called inattentional blindness. Attention works like a spotlight: anything outside the beam, your brain may just not show you.
scenes.imagePrompt: single spotlight beam on an empty dark stage, everything else in darkness, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Would you have spotted the gorilla? Be honest and tell me in the comments.
